record.paper_title: Feynman integrals as generalized functions on path space: things done and open problems
record.original_question: For quantum fields phi, vacuum vector Omega, time-ordering operator T, and a test function f, is the time-ordered vacuum expectation value <Omega, T exp(i phi(f)) Omega> holomorphic as a function of f after continuation from Schwinger functions to the corresponding time-ordered Minkowski functions?

evidence.quote: Time ordered expectation values of quantum fields

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi$ denote a (scalar) quantum field on Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1}$, regarded as an operator-valued tempered distribution acting on a common dense invariant domain in a Hilbert space containing a distinguished vacuum vector $\Omega$. Let $T$ denote the time-ordering operation, and for a real Schwartz test function $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1};\mathbb{R})$ set $\phi(f) = \int \phi(x) f(x)\, dx$. Assume that the theory satisfies the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader framework, so that the associated Euclidean Schwinger $n$-point functions exist and admit analytic continuation to time-ordered Minkowski $n$-point functions, and that the formal generating series
$$ Z(f) \;=\; \bigl\langle \Omega,\; T\, e^{i\phi(f)}\,\Omega \bigr\rangle \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{i^n}{n!} \int \bigl\langle \Omega,\, T\,\phi(x_1)\cdots\phi(x_n)\,\Omega\bigr\rangle\, f(x_1)\cdots f(x_n)\, dx_1\cdots dx_n $$
makes sense (after the Schwinger-to-Minkowski continuation) as a function of $f$ on an appropriate complex neighborhood of $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1};\mathbb{R})$ inside the complexified test-function space $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1};\mathbb{C})$.

Question: Is the time-ordered vacuum expectation value $f \mapsto \bigl\langle \Omega,\, T\, e^{i\phi(f)}\,\Omega \bigr\rangle$ a holomorphic function of $f$ on such a complex neighborhood?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returned general background on Schwinger functions, Osterwalder–Schrader axioms, and analytic continuation, but no source directly establishing or refuting holomorphy of the time-ordered generating functional $\langle\Omega, T e^{i\phi(f)}\Omega\rangle$ in $f$ after continuation from Schwinger to Minkowski functions. The question is posed as an open problem in the surrounding literature on Feynman integrals as generalized functions on path space, and no definitive resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Time-ordered products and Schwinger functions
status_evidence.snippet: Every system of time-ordered products for a local field theory determines a related system of Schwinger functions possessing an extended form of Osterwalder–Schrader positivity, and the converse holds under growth conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Connection between time-ordered products and Schwinger functions is established, but holomorphy of the generating functional in f is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Schwinger function — Grokipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The linear growth condition facilitates the extension of the Schwinger functions to holomorphic functions in suitable tube domains, enabling reconstruction of Wightman distributions.
status_evidence.claim: Holomorphy is established at the level of n-point Schwinger functions on tube domains, not at the level of the full generating functional as a function of the test function f.
